questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

She will be wearing a pink dress to the wedding

options.text: A pink dress would be worn by her to the wedding.
A pink dress would be worn by her at the wedding.
A pink dress will be wear by her to the wedding.
A pink dress will be worn by her to the wedding.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **A pink dress will be worn by her to the wedding.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active form and we need to change it to the passive form.
 
• The given sentence is written in the future continuous tense.
 
• The future continuous tense in the active voice has the following structure: Subject + shall/will + be + V(ing) + object__
 
• The future continuous tense in the passive voice has the following structure: __Object+ shall/will + be + V3 + by subject__
 
• Example - 
 
 
• Active voice - *I will be writing the letter tomorrow.*
 
• Passive voice - *The letter will be written by me tomorrow.*
 
 
 
• Rules of Conversion from Active to Passive Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the subject into an object.
 
• Change the verb into the past participle form.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
 

​Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct Passive Voice: *A pink dress will be worn by her to the wedding.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.**

Rajat said, “I submitted my work assignment yesterday.”

options.text: Rajat said that he had submitted his work assignment yesterday.
Rajat said that he have submitted his work assignment the previous day.
Rajat said that he had submitted his work assignment the previous day.
Rajat said that he submitted his work assignment yesterday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Rajat said that he had submitted his work assignment the previous day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and we need to convert it to indirect speech.
 
• When we change a direct speech to an indirect speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" remains unchanged in the indirect speech.
 
• The inverted commas ("...") are replaced with the conjunction 'that' to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The comma (,) is removed in the indirect speech.
 
• The first word of the indirect speech should be in capital letters.
 
• The first person pronoun "**I**" changes to the third person pronoun "**He**" in the reported speech.
 
• "**My**" changes to "**His**" in the reported speech.
 
• If the direct speech is written in the **simple past** tense, it will be changed into the **past perfect** tense in the indirect speech.
 
• "**Yesterday**" in the direct speech changes to "**the previous day**" in the indirect speech.
 
 
 
• Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

 

Hence, indirect speech is - *Rajat said that he had submitted his work assignment the previous day.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.**

The policeman asked us whether we recognised the person in the photo.

options.text: The policeman said, “Do you recognised the person in the photo.”
The policeman said, “Do you recognise the person in the photo?”
The policeman said, “Did you recognised the person in the photo?”
The policeman said, “Whether you recognise the person in the photo.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The policeman said, “Do you recognise the person in the photo?”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is an indirect speech and we need to convert it to a direct speech.
 
• When we change an indirect speech to a direct speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• The reporting verb "**asked**" changes to "**said**" in the direct speech.
 
• The inverted commas ("...") are placed to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The comma (,) is added after the sentence covered in inverted commas in direct speech.
 
• The first word of the direct speech should be in capital letters.
 
• The plural pronoun 'we' changes to the 2nd person pronoun 'you' in the direct speech.
 
• The **full stop (.)** in the indirect speech changes to the **question mark "?"** in the case of an interrogative sentence.
 
• If the reported speech is written in the past tense it should be changed to the past tense in the reporting speech.
 
• Yes-no question is formed with the use of auxiliary verbs such as – am, is, are, was, were, do, did, can, shall, will, have, has, may.
 
• ‘**Whether**’ is used in the indirect speech for the conversion of yes-no questions in place of "**do**".
 
 
 
• Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

 

Hence, the direct speech is - *The policeman said, “Do you recognise the person in the photo?”*

questions.question:
**Identify the option that rectifies the error in tense in the given sentence.**

The mall just opened and the visitors arrived now.

options.text: The mall is just opening and the visitors are arriving.
The mall just opens and the visitors arrives.
The mall has just been opening and the visitors arrived.
The mall has just opened and the visitors have arrived.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The mall has just opened and the visitors have arrived.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error here lies in the use of tense and we should use the present perfect tense to correct the sentence.
 
• We use the simple past when the action started in the past, finished in the past, and is not continuing now.
 
• But we use the **present perfect** when the action started in the past and is continuing now.
 
• In English, we must always use the present perfect when the time of an action is not important or not specified.
 
 
• **For example-** *They have eaten Thai food.*
 
 
 
• In English, we must always use the simple past when details about the time or place that an action occurred are given or requested.
 
 
• **For example-** *I lived in Amsterdam in 1989.*
 
 
 
• In this sentence the word "**just**" is mentioned which means a very short time before that means that the mall is still open.
 
• So, the present perfect is used to indicate a link between the present and the past when the time of the action is before now.
 
• The structure follows: Subject + have/has + past participle + the rest of the sentence__
 
• The implied meaning of the sentence is: *The emporium has just opened, and customers have begun to appear.*
 
• From here, it is clear that the present perfect tense should be used here in the given sentence.

Hence the correct answer is **option 4.**

**Corrected sentence:** *The mall has just opened and the visitors have arrived.*
